common_name: Cooperi Hibiscus (Variegated Foliage Red-Flowered Tropical Hibiscus)

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings or plant container specimens after all frost risk has passed; Cooperi is grown as much for its striking variegated foliage as for its single red flowers.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, giving some afternoon shade in the hottest climates to preserve the best leaf coloring. Cooperi is one of the oldest and most distinctive tropical hibiscus cultivars, grown as much for its narrow, pointed leaves splashed in green, cream, and pink as for its single scarlet-red flowers, giving the shrub year-round ornamental interest even between bloom flushes. The variegation is often most vivid on new growth and in brighter light, fading somewhat in deep shade. Prune to shape and remove any reverted solid-green shoots, which grow more vigorously than the variegated growth and can overtake the plant if left unchecked; feed with a slow-release fertilizer through the growing season for the best color and bloom.

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings or plant container specimens after all frost risk has passed; President is an old, vigorous tropical hibiscus cultivar grown for its large, reliable red single flowers.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. President bears large, single, classic red flowers with a prominent central staminal column, on a vigorous, fast-growing shrub that has remained a garden favorite for generations thanks to its dependable, near-continuous bloom through the warm season. Its bold, traditional red is a good anchor color for a mixed tropical hibiscus planting, especially alongside the more novel bicolor and pastel cultivars that have become common in recent decades. Prune hard in early spring to encourage vigorous new growth and maximum bloom, and feed with a slow-release fertilizer every four to six weeks through the growing season.

common_name: Agnes Galt Hibiscus (Historic Hawaiian Deep Pink Tropical Hibiscus)

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings or plant container specimens after all frost risk has passed; Agnes Galt is a historic Hawaiian-bred tropical hibiscus cultivar prized for its vigorous, reliable bloom.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Agnes Galt is a historic Hawaiian-bred tropical hibiscus bearing large, single, deep pink flowers in great abundance on a vigorous, upright shrub, a cultivar that helped shape the classic look of tropical hibiscus in mid-20th-century Hawaiian and Gulf Coast gardens. Its reliable, heavy flowering and tough constitution have kept it in cultivation for decades even as flashier modern hybrids have come and gone. Prune hard in early spring to encourage vigorous new growth and maximum bloom, and feed with a slow-release fertilizer every four to six weeks through the growing season.

common_name: Fiesta Hibiscus (Orange-Yellow with Red Veining Tropical Hibiscus)

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings or plant container specimens after all frost risk has passed; Fiesta is a vividly colored tropical hibiscus cultivar with striking red veining over an orange-yellow base.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Fiesta carries large, single flowers in a fiery blend of orange and yellow overlaid with bold red veining radiating out from the throat, a vivid, sunset-toned combination that lives up to its festive name and stands out even among the wide color range typical of tropical hibiscus. Flowers last only a single day, as with all hibiscus, but a well-grown plant produces a steady flush of new buds for continuous color from spring through frost in warm climates. Prune hard in early spring to encourage vigorous new growth and maximum bloom, and feed with a slow-release fertilizer every four to six weeks through the growing season.

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings or plant container specimens after all frost risk has passed; Painted Lady bears soft salmon-pink single flowers on a vigorous tropical hibiscus shrub.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Painted Lady bears large, single flowers in a soft, warm salmon-pink, a gentler and more subdued tone than the bold reds and oranges typical of many tropical hibiscus, making it a good choice for a pastel-themed tropical planting or as a softer accent among brighter companions. It flowers steadily from spring through frost in warm climates, with each individual bloom lasting only a single day before a fresh flush of buds takes its place. Prune hard in early spring to encourage vigorous new growth and maximum bloom, and feed with a slow-release fertilizer every four to six weeks through the growing season.

common_name: Vulcan Hibiscus (Large Ruffled Deep Red Tropical Hibiscus)

planting.note: Root softwood cuttings or plant container specimens after all frost risk has passed; Vulcan bears exceptionally large, deeply ruffled deep red flowers on a vigorous tropical hibiscus shrub.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Vulcan bears exceptionally large, deeply ruffled single flowers in an intense, saturated deep red, among the boldest and most substantial blooms of any commonly grown tropical hibiscus cultivar, opening a striking focal point in the garden even though, as with all hibiscus, each flower lasts only a single day. A well-grown plant produces a steady succession of new buds for continuous color from spring through frost in warm climates. Prune hard in early spring to encourage vigorous new growth and maximum bloom, and feed with a slow-release fertilizer every four to six weeks through the growing season.
